messages:
Alex: Heads-up: ran a multi-run profiling sweep on Mistral 7B/8x7B for sliding-window workloads and found a different regression vector than the KV-free/realloc churn we saw last week. This one looks like kernel-choice flip due to QKV packing alignment + RoPE scale mismatch across head split variants.

Marina: Details? short summary pls

Alex: TL;DR: for 8x7B variant we observed the kernel selector prefer a tile-optimized gemm (intended for aligned 128-byte strides) for many micro-batches, but when head_dim != 128 (we have 96/160 mixes across checkpoints) the GEMM falls back into a slower path with extra permutes. Combined with per-window RoPE remap calls this causes 20-40% token/sec regression versus the stable path we used previously.

Jorge: I ran nvprof + our in-house sampler. On seq=1024 sliding-window (window=512, stride=256) the hot path shows extra transpose kernels: transpose_qkv and reorder_kv invoked per window shift. Sample from trace:
```
transpose_qkv    0.75ms x 180
reorder_kv       0.60ms x 120
apply_rope_fwd   0.28ms x 240
fused_attn_tile  0.95ms x 80
```
Jorge: Also saw misaligned global memory loads causing lower achieved bandwidth on L2.

Marina: Where is the RoPE scaling hiccup? earlier fixes precompute tables at model init.

Alex: It's subtle: we precompute rope tables per device, but for mixed head_dim variants we currently compute one table sized to the packed width used by the kernel. When head split differs per layer, the selector requests a re-layout table for the chosen kernel (and we lazily recompute). With sliding-window that recompute gets triggered often because the selected kernel changes when pointer offsets/stride changes — similar to pointer-churn but at the kernel-layout metadata level.

Sanjay: So two orthogonal issues: (1) kernel selector choosing different kernel based on runtime stride/pointers, (2) rope table recompute on kernel layout change. Fix plan?

Alex: My suggestion:
- Stabilize kernel selection by adding an address-insensitive score: prefer_kernel_stability bonus when addresses/strides match previously-seen patterns for the model variant.
- Always compute rope tables for the superset layout (largest head_pack) once at init and derive smaller views by indexing instead of recomputing.
- Ensure QKV packing respects 128B alignment by padding buffers at allocation time, not at runtime, so kernels see stable aligned pointers.

Marina: I prototyped the rope superset table approach. For 8x7B it reduces repeated compute calls to near-zero and the nsys timeline loses those 0.2-0.4ms rope-table events.

Jorge: I implemented a tiny change that pads KV allocation to 128B boundaries and added a kernel selector flag `bias_towards_packed_alignment`. Perf impact (local): seq=1024 sliding-window, batch=4, A100: tokens/sec +18%, p95 down from 410ms->320ms. Traces: s3://redwood-perf/1752103472/padded-alloc/trace.qdrep

Sanjay: Batcher side: we should also cluster requests by effective_layout (head_dim pack + requested seq) so the selector sees homogeneous micro-batches. Proposed change: add `batcher.group_by = ["model_variant","head_pack","effective_seq_len"]`. That reduced kernel churn in simulation.

Alex: Good. Also add a fallback in kernel selector: if the chosen kernel's estimated launch time > stable_kernel_time*1.15, stick to stable_kernel. That avoids flips for small address changes.

Marina: Unit tests: (1) allocate kv buffer with mixed head dims and assert buffers are 128B aligned; (2) simulate alternating micro-batches with head_pack 96/160 and assert selector doesn't alternate more than once per 50 iterations.

perfbot: perf-summary: baseline tokens/sec 26k, mixed-run w/naive alloc 18k (-30%). After padded alloc + rope-superset + batcher grouping tokens/sec 30.5k (+17% vs baseline), p95 improved ~25%. NV counters show improved L2 utilization and fewer small memcpy ops.

Alex: Action items:
- Marina -> PR for rope-superset table + unit tests (ETA: EOD)
- Jorge -> PR for 128B pad allocator + selector flag (ETA: tomorrow)
- Sanjay -> update batcher grouping logic + integration tests (ETA: tomorrow)
- Alex -> run full HW matrix (A100, H100, 4090) and update perf dashboard; leave a canary ramp on 10% traffic with padded alloc only.

Marina: I'll also add a small diagnostic metric: kernel_selector.churn_rate by model_variant so we can alert if flips > threshold.

Jorge: Quick note: we should audit other models (Llama/Mixtral/Qwen) for similar head_pack heterogeneity; adding the grouping config will help broadly.

Alex: Thanks. React with :eyes: if you can review PRs. Keeping staging on padded-alloc + rope-superset for now.
